title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool + parallel calls with robust result injection and retry semantics
author: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics for sequences that require multiple tools and parallel tool invocations. This change standardizes how tool results are injected back into the model prompt/state, adds deterministic retry/backoff semantics for failed tool invocations, and preserves streaming stability when tool calls are interleaved with partial outputs. Motivation: customers are using complex tool graphs (e.g., call 3 enrichment services in parallel, then synthesize results). The previous behavior produced non-deterministic injections, awkward partial streaming, and no first-class retry semantics which caused flakes in production. Goals: 1) Allow callers to declare multi-tool invocations and receive an ordered, deterministic injection stream. 2) Support parallel execution with configurable concurrency and failure isolation. 3) Provide automatic retries with exponential backoff for transient tool failures, while exposing retry metadata to the user. 4) Keep streaming output stable and compatible with existing OpenAI-compatible tool-calling patterns. Design: - New execution plan stage: ToolInvocationPlan (internal-only) which flattens multi-tool calls and annotates ordering/isolation hints. - Injection strategy: canonicalize tool results into a 'tool_result' delta token stream that can be inserted as a single atomic unit into the completion stream; this prevents partial outputs from being interleaved with model generation. - Parallelism control: new request options: tool_concurrency (int) and tool_isolation (enum: "shared_context"|"isolated_context"). Default behavior: tool_concurrency=3, tool_isolation=shared_context. - Retry semantics: per-tool retry_policy with fields: max_attempts, backoff_base_ms, retry_on (list). Retries are handled by the runtime caller layer and surfaced in the response metadata. - Streaming compatibility: during streaming, we emit placeholders for in-flight tool calls ("[tool:weather|pending]") and then emit an atomic replacement once tool result is available. This keeps SSE/event stream shape stable. Backwards compatibility: - Existing OpenAI-compatible tool-calling semantics remain available via compatibility flag openai_compat: true. When enabled, we map the new structured injection into the legacy "function_call"/"function_response" pattern. Implementation notes: - Changes across layers: api-gateway (new request params parsing), runtime orchestration (ToolInvocationPlan, parallel executor), model-runtime connector (atomic injection point), SDK helpers (python/ts SDK updated helpers to construct per-tool retry policies). - Added telemetry: tool_call.attempts, tool_call.latency_ms, tool_call.retry_count, tool_call.failure_reason. - Tests: end-to-end integration tests that simulate flakey tool endpoints and assert deterministic injection ordering; unit tests for retry/backoff; streaming smoke tests to ensure SSE events maintain shape. Checklist: - [x] Design doc + tradeoffs (linked in PR) - [x] SDK updates for Python/TS - [x] Runtime executor + unit tests - [x] Integration tests with streaming harness - [x] Telemetry and alerts updated - [x] Backcompat layer (openai_compat) - [x] Docs snippet + changelog Notes: Performance: in internal perf runs this adds ~6-10ms median overhead for simple single-tool calls (mostly from bookkeeping) and improves latency tail for multi-tool flows by reducing flush-induced stalls. Rollout: feature default enabled for new API version v1.11; openai_compat remains default for older API versions.

review_comments: Tomás Rivera: Nice design. Two concerns: (1) Can we keep injection atomicity but avoid copying large payloads for >1MB tool results? (2) Need clear signal for callers when a tool is retried multiple times so they can surface UX.

Aisha Patel: (reply) For (1) we stream-by-reference where possible (we emit a stable object handle instead of copying payload into the prompt); added core/runtime/atomic_injector.cpp path that implements reference streaming. For (2) we added tool_call.attempts and tool_call.retry_count in response metadata and SDK surfaces an event when a retry occurs.
Mei Chen: tests look solid. Please add a unit test for the isolation mode where tools run in isolated_context and ensure no shared KV cache leakage.
Aisha Patel: Added isolated_context unit test and an extra assert in the cache manager.
